title: DoorDash Cuts Grocery Reorder Latency from 16 to 2 Seconds with AI Agents
gist: DoorDash cut AI grocery-reorder latency from about 16 to 2 seconds by precomputing recurring purchases with batch LLM inference and resolving against the live catalog at request time, lifting order rate about 34%.

insights.claim: DoorDash cut grocery reorder latency from about 16 seconds to 2 seconds by precomputing recurring purchase needs rather than rebuilding them per request.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Moving reasoning offline is a practical lever on LLM-product latency and cost.

insights.claim: The faster flow doubled shopping list views and raised the flow's order rate by approximately 34%.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Direct evidence that latency improvements convert to revenue in consumer AI.
insights.locator: The change doubled shopping list views

insights.claim: The pipeline runs batch LLM inference on 90 days of purchase history plus profile signals, validates outputs deterministically, then resolves items against the live catalog by store item, product ID, then search term.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Hybrid batch-LLM plus deterministic validation is a template for production agents.
insights.locator: For grocery reordering, DoorDash processes 90 days

insights.claim: The design principle is deciding what belongs in the agent loop and what can happen ahead of time; simple edits skip the LLM while the Grocery agent handles reasoning-heavy requests like cheaper alternatives.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Selective LLM invocation reduces inference spend.
insights.quote: Better agentic systems aren’t always about more reasoning; they’re about deciding what belongs in the agent loop and what can happen ahead of time.

insights.claim: DoorDash's shared agent platform provides orchestration, memory, model access, tracing, evaluation and rollout controls, and adding the Reservations agent took one week, about ten times faster than the first domain agents.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Shared platform amortization speeds up agent rollout across domains.

insights.claim: The shopping list is a structured artifact both consumer and agent edit, and a consumer's direct edit is authoritative over earlier conversation.
insights.speaker: Leela Kumili
insights.so_what: Structured shared state improves reliability versus chat-history reliance.
insights.quote: A consumer’s direct edit is authoritative: the next agent turn starts from the edited list, not from what was said earlier.
